cover.title: Al Capone said something was in his cell

lines.text: In 1929, the most feared gangster in America was locked inside this prison... and the story goes, something followed him into his cell.
Philadelphia. Eastern State Penitentiary. It opened in 1829, built like a castle, with cell blocks spreading out like the spokes of a wheel.
The idea was total solitude. Prisoners lived alone, ate alone, and worked alone... for years.
Then Al Capone arrived. He spent eight months here. His first prison sentence.
His cell had rugs, lamps, and a radio. But he didn't sleep well.
Legend says guards heard him at night, begging someone to leave him alone. Capone believed it was a man killed in the Saint Valentine's Day Massacre.
The prison closed in 1971. Today it's open for tours.
And in Cellblock 12, staff and visitors report voices and laughter echoing down an empty hall.
If you hear him tonight... comment leave him alone. Sleep tight, partner.
